--- title: "08 — DARM calibration via Pintelon–Schoukens" description: "The same multisine pipeline applied to the gravitational-wave readout: one Pcal multisine recovers the DARM response R(f) and the sensing function C leakage-free, per-stage drives recover the actuation strengths, and a swept sine is run head-to-head on the same twin." image: thumbnails/08.svg categories: [calibration, closed-loop, DARM] freeze: true --- ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} ## What you'll learn - The multisine pipeline applied to the **gravitational-wave readout** (DARM). - Recovering the sensing function and per-stage actuation, leakage-free. ::: [![Launch in Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/CaltechExperimentalGravity/system_ident/HEAD?urlpath=lab/tree/docs/examples/08-darm-calibration.ipynb) · run this page live (no install; the [in-browser demo](interactive.qmd) is instant) The earlier examples identify suspensions. This one identifies the **gravitational-wave readout itself** — the DARM loop a LIGO calibration group characterises every run. The method does not change: a periodic multisine, a leakage-free reference FRF, a measured per-bin noise model, and a Cramér–Rao envelope. Only the plant is new: a closed loop with a sensing function `C`, three-stage actuation `A`, and a digital servo `D`, under **both** process disturbance and readout noise. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Representative, not a specific interferometer The twin uses representative Advanced-LIGO numbers — a coupled-cavity pole near 360 Hz, a ~77 µs delay, three pendulum-stage actuators, and a UGF≈50 Hz loop. It is a *demonstration* of the measurement, not a calibration of any real instrument. The page is rendered with `freeze: true`. ::: ::: {#63768174 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Setup — import the presentation glue"} import sys, pathlib _p = pathlib.Path.cwd() for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]: if (_c / "docs" / "darm_demo.py").exists() and str(_c / "docs") not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c / "docs")) if (_c / "darm_demo.py").exists() and str(_c) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_c)) import numpy as np import darm_demo as dd ``` ::: ## The loop and what calibration delivers DARM strain is `h = R·d_err/L` with response `R = (1+G)/C` and open-loop gain `G = A·D·C`. The calibration job is to know `R(f)` — and, underneath it, the sensing `C` and the three actuation strengths — to ~1 % in magnitude and ~1° in phase across the band. ::: {#4fe1407c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="The twin's truth — C, A, G, R"} dd.truth_fig() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## One Pcal multisine — what you'd watch A single periodic multisine injected at Pcal, ramped on and off over 3 s, with the DARM error read out under the loop's real disturbance and readout noise. ::: {#37d35b69 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Raw Pcal measurement — drive in, d_err out"} a = dd.pcal_audit(seed=1) dd.pcal_timeseries_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The leakage-free FRF `d_err/x_pc = C/(1+G)` with its per-line coherence, on the analytic truth: ::: {#80bbf63b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Leakage-free FRF + coherence"} dd.pcal_bode_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## The deliverable: R(f), model-free Because `d_err/x_pc = C/(1+G)`, the response is simply its reciprocal — `R(f) = 1/FRF`, with no model in the loop. Its CRB envelope falls straight out of the FRF's per-bin error. ::: {#f649bea2 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Recovered R(f) ± CRB vs truth"} dd.response_envelope_fig(a) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Underneath: the sensing function C Multiplying the FRF by the (known, designed) loop factor `(1+G)` exposes the optical sensing `C`; a weighted complex fit returns the optical gain, the coupled-cavity pole, and the delay. ::: {#f5d7a3ec .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Sensing fit — g_C, f_cc, τ"} from IPython.display import display display(dd.sensing_table(a)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Sensing function C — representative truth vs P&S recovery** | sensing parameter | true | recovered | σ (CRB) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | optical gain g_C [ct/m] | 1e+06 | 1e+06 | 3.2e+02 | | cavity pole f_cc [Hz] | 360.00 | 359.93 | 0.18 | | delay τ [µs] | 77.0 | 77.0 | 0.07 | ::: ::: ## The actuation strengths, Pcal as the ruler A Pcal-only measurement cannot separate the three stages (they live inside `G` as a product). Driving each stage in turn and dividing by the Pcal FRF removes `C/(1+G)`, leaving `κ_i N_i` referenced to the absolute Pcal meter — so each `κ` comes back on its own. ::: {#3186bacf .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Recover κ_U / κ_PU / κ_T"} d = dd.actuation_campaign(seed=2) display(dd.actuation_table(d)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Actuation strengths κ — Pcal as the absolute ruler** | stage | true κ | recovered κ | σ (CRB) | |Δ| | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | UIM | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.00052 | 0.01% | | PUM | 0.400 | 0.400 | 0.00045 | 0.02% | | TST | 0.080 | 0.080 | 0.00084 | 0.26% | ::: ::: ## Head-to-head with the swept sine Same twin, same disturbance + readout noise, same total wall-clock. The multisine measures every bin at once; the swept sine spends the clock one frequency at a time, so in equal time it reaches only a handful of frequencies (each tight, because it spends full power there) — and covering the whole band to the same uncertainty costs it ~100× longer. Shown on the same twin, not asserted. ::: {#9dbb6582 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="σ(R)/|R| — multisine (whole band) vs swept sine (few points), equal wall-clock"} c = dd.comparison(seed=0) dd.comparison_fig(c) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#2fa2a246 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Where the methods differ"} display(dd.fom_table(c)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} **Where the multisine method differs for DARM (representative; the efficiency is shown above, not asserted)** | figure of merit | swept sine | P&S multisine | | --- | --- | --- | | Frequencies per measurement | 1 (dwell) | all band bins at once | | Leakage | windowed / settle each point | leakage-free (periodic) | | Noise model | assumed / averaged | per-bin, from period-to-period variance | | Budget allocation | uniform / manual | CRB-optimal (Fisher-matched) | | Loop handling | model out the servo | FRF cancels it (reference-based) | | Time for full-band coverage | ≈99 min | 16 s (one window) | ::: ::: ## Honest gaps This twin is a single DARM loop with a one-pole sensing function and static strengths. It omits the optical spring / SRC detuning, time-dependent coefficients (TDCF tracking lines — though [example 13](13-darm-drift-tracking.qmd) now tracks a drifting strength κ(t) directly), and the cross-couplings of a real interferometer. The efficiency claim above is a *demonstration on a twin*; the real test is to run both injections on the same instrument state and compare the `σ(R(f))`-per-hour envelopes — see `notes/darm-calibration-via-pns.md`. ## Roadmap The through-line never changes — a periodic multisine, a leakage-free reference FRF, a maximum-likelihood fit toward the Cramér–Rao bound. Each step below raises the *twin's* fidelity toward a real DARM calibration, keeping that one method. **Done** - **Static single-loop calibration** (this page). Sensing `C`, three-stage actuation `κ`, the response `R(f)` with a measured CRB envelope, and a swept-sine head-to-head on the same twin. - **Round 1 — track a drifting parameter** ([example 13](13-darm-drift-tracking.qmd)). A known slow drift on the ESD strength `κ(t)`, recovered with a Lataire–Pintelon time-basis fit inside an honest CRB band, with resolvability proven by a computed bound rather than eyeballed. **Next — raising fidelity, roughly in order** 1. **Realistic drift** — replace the deterministic profile with a stochastic (GP) wander at a physical correlation time; score the recovery statistically. 2. **SRC-detuning optical spring** — replace the single real sensing pole with an optical biquad parametrized on the physical detuning `φ`, so the DARM pole migrates **real → complex** as `φ` drifts (the crossing stays analytic in `φ`). 3. **Several parameters at once** — the optical gain, the cavity-pole / detuning, and the stage `κ_i` drifting jointly, not one scalar in isolation. 4. **One-shot Lataire–Pintelon fit** — fit the time-basis coefficients directly to the record, alongside today's two-step snapshot form, as a cross-check. 5. **Continuous TDCF lines** — always-on calibration lines tracking `κ(t)` between full sweeps, the operational counterpart to the snapshot campaign. 6. **The actuation / DAC chain** — whitening / de-whitening and coil-driver shaping with a pre-injection saturation check at the DAC, plus ESD charge / voltage limits. 7. **Real filters & couplings** — import real DARM / actuation filter shapes and the interferometer cross-couplings (MIMO), toward a calibration of an actual instrument state. Live-CDS / hardware injection is a separate, later phase. The full design and citations live in `notes/darm-calibration-via-pns.md`.
